card.name: Words leading into effect or action
card.fires_on: Words just before a noun like effect, action, relief or adjustment, such as increased, prompt, demand(s), greater, requires. Mostly in dosing text about how much benefit or speed is needed.

modes.label: Increased or greater effect
modes.description: A modifier right before the word effect when saying more drug gives no added benefit.
modes.example: does not produce an<< increased>> effect.

modes.label: Need for prompt action
modes.description: A verb or adjective saying the situation calls for fast treatment or adjustment.
modes.example: unless the clinical situation<< demands>> more rapid adjustment.

modes.label: Other linking words before effects
modes.description: Small words such as no, the, or without before an outcome term.
modes.example: clinically effective in most patients<< without>> the production of appreciable side effects.

card.writes: Pushes toward intensity words like pronounced and rising, and away from practical or code-like pieces.
card.plain: It marks the spot in dosing text where the next word will be about the size of an effect or how quickly action is needed.
